messages.subject: "Bug" in MVN rng
parts:
Hi!

I just discovered a "bug" in the MVN random number generator. The function does not stop the user from sampling even if the covariance matrix is not positive semi-definite. Attached is an example. I know users who provide wrong input are bad, but it happens - so you might consider adding a check here.

Best,
Sebastian

Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] "Bug" in MVN rng
parts:
On Sep 24, 2014, at 3:25 AM, Sebastian Weber <sdw....@gmail.com> wrote:

> What's the problem with multi_normal_rng?
>
> Efficiency? I don't care always...
> Accuracy? I might care, given how bad the function performs.
>

Both. We're moving to try to parameterize multivariates
in terms of their Cholesky factors rather than their covariance
or precision matrices. It helps for both efficiency and arithmetic
stability.
> I suppose you suggest to use cholesky factors and sample standard normal variates instead, but then why shouldn't I let the multi_normal_rng do this work for me?

If you absolutely must have a covariance matrix parameterization,
then it's just a matter of efficiency whether you let multi_normal_rng
do the work or you do the work. Doing it yourself, you can factor once
on the outside. When we allow multi_normal_rng to return multiple
draws, then that motiviation would go away.

> I saw your tickets and I agree that having a function which outputs a vector would be very nice. In fact the function could figure out itself from the vector I have on the LHS how many random numbers I want, that would be really cool.

That's not possible. Stan is purely compositional in that expressions
are evaluated only based on their sub-expressions, not based on the
context in which they occur. I feel pretty strongly about maintaining
that property. It's still compatible with conversions/promotions of
output (e.g., assigning an int to a real, which I really want to push
through cointainers everywhere if I can figure out how to do it).

- Bob
